FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, the Rotating Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by Council. after the draft finalized by the Electrotechnical Division

This is a comprehensive standard covering generators coupled to internal combustion engines of machines intended for special without distinction of output and voltage, with the exception applications, such as machines for traction vehicles, marine service and air transport. 3) dusts/fumes of explosives, 4) flammable gases, 5) lint, 6) nuclear radiation, 7) oil vapour, 8) salt air, and 9) steam. b) Operation in mines, entirely enclosed boxes, poorly ventilated rooms, damp or very dry places. c) Operation at speeds other than rated (this excludes normal overspeed).

3.3 Load All the numerical values of the electrical and mechanical quantities that signify the demand to be made on a rotating machine by an electrical circuit or a mechanism at a given instant. 3.4 Rated Output The apparent electric power available at terminals expressed in. volt-amperes or kilo volt amperes together with the specified power factor frequency and voltage. 3.5 No Load
The state of a machine rotating at normal speed under

3.10 Excitation Voltage The voltage marked on the rating plate of a machine and required for excitation at rated output. 3.11 Efficiency
The ratio of output power to the input power (ex-

pressed as a percentage). i.e. Efficiency = Power Output of Machine Power Output of Machine + Power Loss in the Machine

These are intended to prove the general qualities and design of a given type of machine. 3.14 Voltage Terms
These terms describe a generator under the control of

in per unit or percentage of rated output. 3.6.1. Sustained Overload An overload sustained for a sufficiently long period to affect appreciably the temperature of the machine. 3.6.2 Momentary
Overload

An overload the duration of which is so short as not to affect appreciably the temperature of the machine.

The line-to-line voltage at the terminals of the generator at rated output.

3.143 No Load Voltage (UJ
The line-to-line voltage at the terminals of the generator at rated frequency and at no load.

The maximum change in voltage expressed as per-

Statement of the load including no load, rest and deenergized period to which the machine is subjected including their duration and sequence in time. 3.8 Duty Type Aconventionalperiodicdutyconsistingofoneormore sets of loads remaining constant for the durations specified. 3.9 Thermal Equilibrium The state reached when the observed temperature rises of the several parts of the machine do not vary by more than 2.0% over a period of one hour. 2

centage of the rated voltage, when the load changes from rated load at rated voltage, speed and power factor to any lower load, including no load, without change in speed and excitation current, taking into account the effect on governor and automatic voltage regulation. 3.145 Transient Voltage Deviation (R,U) Maximumdeviationofvoltageafterasuddenspecified load change from a voltage previous to steady state level at rated speed and specified power factor. 3.14.6 Voltage Recovery Time (zu) The time interval from the point when the' voltage departs from the specified steady state voltage

IS 13364 (Part 2) : 1992 regulation band after a load change until the voltage again returns to and remains within this band. 3.14.7 Voltage Regulation Characteristics (-)

a) The common voltage differing from its rated value by not more than +5 percent, or b) The frequency differing from its rated value by not more than 23 percent, or c) Any combination of (a) and (b). In the case of operation at extreme voltage limits, the temperature rise limits specified in 11 shall not exceed by more than 5%. Machines when operated under the abnormal conditions of voltage and frequency variation may not necessarily have their performance in accordance with this standard. 5 TYPE OF ENCLOSURES For machines covered by this standard, the specification for types of enclosures shall be as given in IS 4691 : 1985. 6 COOLING SYSTEMS The machines covered by this standard shall have one of the cooling systems.given in IS 6362 : 1971. 7 PREFERRED AND OUTPUTS
VOLTAGES, FREQUENCY

Curves of terminal voltage as a function of load current at given power factor rated and frequency. 3.148 Voltage Modulation (Modulation Amplitude) c,o, Voltage modulation is a quasi&periodic voltage variation about a steady state voltage at frequencies below the fundamental of service frequency expressed as a percentage of the rated voltage at rated frequency and uniform drive. 3.14.9 Angular Displacement of Polyjhzse System NJ Electrical angular displacement of the generator phase voltage vector relative to the corresponding phase voltage vector of a symmetrical polyphase system (with three phase system 1200 at virtually nondeforming and virtually balanced loads between no load and rated load, expressed in electrical degrees). 3.14.10 Maximum Voltage Unbalance (6~) The maximum voltage unbalance is the ratio of the negative sequence or the zero sequence voltage components to the positive sequence voltage components at no load. 4 SITE CONDITIONS 4.0 The following shall constitute the normal site conditions. 4.1 Altitude and Temperature Machines shall be designed for the following site conditions unless otherwise agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 4.1.1 Altitude Altitude not xceeding 1 OOOmetres.Machines intended for service on sites where the altitude is in excess of 1000 me&s are covered in 6.3 of IS 12802 : 1989. 4.1.2 Temperature The cooling air or gas temperature not exceeding WC. 7.1 Preferred Voltages

For the purpose of this standard, the preferred voltages shall be in accordance with IS 12360 : 1988. 7.2 Frequency and Number of Phases For AC generators the frequency shall be the standard frequency of 50 Hz. 7.4.1 The standard number of phases for AC generators shall be three or one.

8 IRREGULARITIES

OR WAVEFORM

8.1 The generators to this standard shall meet any one of the requirements covered under 8.3,8.4 and 8.5. If none are stated by the purchaser during enquiry, requirements shall apply. The waveform measurement shall be done on open circuit rated voltage at rated speed. 8.2 Non Linear Loads The non linear loads (thyrister loads) introduce harmonics in the alternator armature current. This in fact disturbs the generator voltage waveform which may lead to malfunctioning of the system. A standard alternator may supply 20 to 40 percent non linear loads along with conventional loads, may be of 80 to 60 percent depending upon the design of thyrister panel and alternatorparameters. However, this has tobe done by an agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 4

It is recommended that users of all:matos inform the generator manufacturer whenever thyrister loads or furnace loads are encountered. 8.3 Telephone Harmonic The requirements 8.4 Waveform Factor

will the

will be as per 9.1 of IS 4722 : 1992. Deviation

The line-to-line voltage waveform shall be obtained with the generator running at rated voltage at normal speed and on open circuit on an oscillographic recorder. The rms value of the voltage is also measured, a sinusoidal voltage waveform of the fundamental computed from the rms value is superposed on the recorded waveform. The waveform deviation is expressed as the difference in any of the instantaneous values of the actual waveform recorded and the sinusoidal waveform of fundamental to the peak value of fundamental.

IS 13364 (Part 2) : 1992 Waveform deviation (percent) = where c = peak value of fundamental. The waveform deviation will not exceed the following limits :

12 OVERLOAD 12.1 Momentary Excess Current for Generators

Above 20 kVA and up to 300 kVA Above 300 kVA and up to 1250 kVA

10 percent 8 percent

A generator rated in accordance with this standard shall be capable of withstanding for not less than 15 seconds, a current 50 percent in excess of its rated current after having attained the thermal equilibrium corresponding to the rated load, the voltage being maintained as near the rated value as possible consistent with the maximum capacity of the prime mover. The exact value of the voltage is not important. 12.2 Exciters The exciters shallbe capable of deliveringthe required excitation current for overloads specified in 12.1. 12.2.1 The exciters shall be rated 1.25 times the full load (1 ted) conditions.

9 DUTY 9.1 The generators covered by this standard shall be of continuous duty unless specified otherwise by the purchaser. Other duties can be specified as per one of the requimmentr in IS 4722 : 1992. The manufacturer may select a suitable machine from his standard list to meet this duty, based on data supplied by the purchaser.
10 EARTHING

15.1 The purchaser shall specify the rated conditions in terms of voltage, output kVA, power factor and speed. The efficiency shall be determined by inputoutput method or any method specified in IS 4889 : 1968. The voltage regulation shall be calculated in accordance with 3.14.4. The tolerances applicable to the determined values of efficiency and voltage regulation shall be according to 16.

15.1.1 In case of brushless generators, the efficiency may be determined by assuming the design value'of the mainfield current and the design efficiency value of exciters.
16 TOLERANCES

Earthing of the machine shall be done in accordance with the relevant provisions of IS 3043 : 1987.
11 TEMPERATURE RISE LIMITS

The generators to this standard shall meet the limits of temperature rise covered in IS 4722 : 1992.

IS 13364 (Fart 2) : 1992 20.1.4 Certificates of all type tests together with a record of alterations whether essential or not, which have been made to the machine since the tests were carried out, shall be kept available by the manufacturer for inspection. 20.2 The procedures laid out in IS 7132 : 1973 and IS 7306 : 1974 for testing the generators other than single phase and evalutating the machine parameters will in general apply to the generators covered by this standard. 20.3 Synchronours 203.1 Type Tests The following shall constitute the type tests: Generators 21 HIGH VOLTAGE TEST High voltage test will be conducted on the machine with exciter as per IS 4722 : 1992. 22 INSULATION RESISTANCE TEST The test requirements and the procedure shall be in accordance with IS 4722 : 1992. 23 OVERSPEED 23.1 All machines shall be designed to withstand a speed of 1.2 times the rated speed unless specified otherwise. 23.2 An overspeed test is not normally considered necessary but may be performed when this is specified and has been agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser at the time of the order. An overspeed test shall be considered as satisfactory is no permanent abnormal deformation is apparent subsequently and no other weakness is detected which may prevent the machine from operating normally and provided the rotor windings after the test comply with the required dielectric tests. The duration of any overspeed test shall be two minutes. 23.3 Due to settling in laminated rotor rims, laminated poles held by wedges or by bolts, etc, a minute permanent increase in the diameter is natural and not to be considered as an abnormal deformation indicating that the machine is not suitable for normal operation. 24 UNBALANCED LOAD Unless otherwise specified three-phase synchronous generators of ratings up to 1 250 kVA shall be capable of continuously operating on an unbalanced load (as defined in 3.6.4) of 25 percent with none of the phase currents exceeding the rated current. The temperature rise limits specified in IS 4722 : 1992 may exceed by 10�C when generator operation under such conditions. The voltage regulation under the above condition will not apply. 25 SHORT-CIRCUIT CURRENT

The following shall constitute the routine tests: Measurement of resistance, Insulation resistance test, Phase sequence test (for 3-phase generators only), Regulation test; Measurement of open circuit characteristic, Measurement of short-circuit characteristic, and High voltage test. 7

Unless otherwise specified, the peak value of the shortcircuit current for synchronous machines, in the case of short circuit on all phases during operation at rated voltage, shall not exceed 15 times the peak value or 21 times the rms value of the rated current. `Ihe check may be carried out by calculation or by means of a test at a voltage of 50 percent of the rated voltage or above.
NOTE The short-circuit current value can be more for alternators supplying non-linear loads ( see 8.2 ).

SHORT-CIRCUIT 26 INSTANTANEOUS WITHSTAND TEST FOR AC GENERATORS 26.1 `Ihe short-circuit test for AC generators shall be carried out only at the express request of the purchaser made at the time of the order. In this case, the test shall be carried out on the machine running on no load with an excitation corresponding to the rated foltage unless otherwise agreed. In no case shall the test be carried out

IS 13364(part 2) : 1992 with an excitation greater than that corresponding 1.05 times the rated voltage. to Specifications for carbon brushes IS 3003 (parts 14% 2) for electric machines IS 3043 : 1987 Code of practice for earthing (first revision ) Degree of protection provided by enclosures for rotating electrical machinery (first revision ) Rotating electrical machines

26.1.1 This voltage may be reduced by agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser in order to take into account the impedance of the transformer which may be placed between the generators and the system. In the latter case, it may be requested that the test be made on the site with the over excitation device in service. The short circuit shall be maintained for 3 seconds. 26.2 The test is considered satisfactory if no harmful deformation occurs and if the requirements of the high voltage test are met after the short-circuit test. 27 RADIO INTERFERENCE SUPPRESSION

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
